text: D6's acceptance says to verify both BH and e-BH against hand-calculated p-values, but the cited e-BH guarantee is for valid e-values (nonnegative variables with null expectation <=1), not arbitrary p-values. The test clause neither supplies e-values nor specifies a p-to-e calibration or null-validity proof, so it cannot substantiate e-BH's arbitrary-dependence guarantee. The bead's own Math Review notes the valid-input-type requirement, but the runnable acceptance still names p-values.
evidence: var/agent-tmp/converge/r4/issues.jsonl:180 (jev-b35c.25 acceptance, D6); https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.02824 (abstract: e-values have expectation at most one under the null; e-BH controls FDR for any dependence)
fix: Separate method fixtures and contracts: BH gets valid p-values under a declared independence/PRDS regime (or a justified dependence-robust procedure); e-BH gets valid e-values with explicit family/batch boundaries. Add a dependence-violating p-value negative and assert invalid/mismatched inputs refuse rather than count as evidence.

text: The SWE-bench citation does not support the stated 40% repeated-failed-command rate. Its 40% figure is the share of benchmark instances with at least two fail-to-pass tests, not the share of agent turns spent on repeated failed commands. The local 8,948 post-error-decision count establishes volume, not that 40% rate.
evidence: var/agent-tmp/converge/r4/issues.jsonl:627 (jev-n4-recover-error-rule-1grh.1 description); https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06770 section 2.3: 40% of instances have at least two fail-to-pass tests
fix: Remove the SWE-bench attribution and 40% statistic. Use a locally measured identical-retry rate with its denominator and sampling window, or state the observed local decision count as volume only and treat the retry-waste hypothesis as unmeasured.
